title: A registry for constants added at run time

blocks.text: An enum's constants are fixed when it is compiled: `new` on an enum is a compile error, and reflection refuses to create one. When new "constants" must arrive at run time (from a plug-in or a configuration file), the course's workaround is a registry: named values that behave like enum constants, but can be added later.

items: `void register(String name, T value)` adds an entry. A name already taken is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`, and its first value stays.
`T get(String name)` returns the value registered under `name`, and throws `NoSuchElementException` when there is none (never `null`).
`List<String> names()` lists the names in **registration order**, the way `values()` lists constants in declaration order.

blocks.text: Names reach the registry from outside (a file, a request), so a name passed to `get` is often a different `String` object from the one registered.

cases.says: An entry registered under a name is found by that name, and size() counts the entries.
Registering a name a second time throws IllegalArgumentException and keeps the first value.
get() of a name nobody registered throws NoSuchElementException instead of returning null.
names() lists the names in the order they were registered, like values() lists constants in declaration order.
get() finds an entry by a name that was built at run time, not written as the same literal.

concepts: An enum's constants are fixed at compile time, so values that must be added at run time need a registry instead.
